content.title: About
content.content: A cream puff (eclair) is a small choux pastry filled with custard or whipped cream and topped with icing. This version is made with reduced fat, using less butter and low‑fat milk, while preserving the light, airy texture and delicate flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic French eclair gets its name from the lightning‑fast way it disappears at bakeries.
Choux pastry is leavened by steam, not yeast, giving it a hollow interior perfect for filling.
Reduced‑fat recipes replace part of the butter with vegetable oil and use skimmed milk in the cream.
Eclairs are a popular party treat because they can be easily glazed in many colors.
In Russia, cream‑filled pastries are often enjoyed with fruit jams or chocolate glaze.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Eggs in the choux dough provide high‑quality protein essential for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains calcium
items.content: Low‑fat milk in the filling supplies calcium for bone health.

items.title: Lower saturated fat
items.content: Reducing butter cuts saturated fat, supporting heart‑friendly nutrition.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and dairy contribute B2, B12 and folate, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Moderate sugar level
items.content: The recipe uses a modest amount of sugar, helping to keep blood‑glucose spikes in check.

items.title: Egg and milk allergy
items.content: People allergic to eggs or dairy should avoid this product.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Despite reduced fat, the pastry still contains sugar, so diabetics should monitor portions.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Lower fat reduces calories, but a single puff can still be energy‑dense.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The wheat flour base contains gluten, making it unsuitable for those with celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Eat cream puffs by hand as a dessert or snack. Pair them with fresh berries, fruit sauce, or a cup of tea. For extra indulgence, drizzle a light glaze on top.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep puffs in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer freshness, refrigerate for up to 5 days. Allow them to come to room temperature before serving.
